D008-D001_h024.question: "Lately, it's like I'm on a seesaw, and I can't get off. For about two months, I was just buzzing, you know? My mind was racing, and I was full of ideas for the hotel. I even started several new projects at once, trying to revamp everything from the catering menu to the concierge system. I poured a lot of money into some new ventures, things I was sure would be brilliant, even though, looking back, they were probably pretty reckless. I was snapping at everyone, too, my staff, vendors—just truly irritable. But for the past three months, it's like a different person. I can barely get myself to start anything, even things I know need doing. My brain feels foggy, like I'm walking through a daze all the time. Sleep is a nightmare; I wake up constantly and then just stare at the ceiling. Sometimes, out of nowhere, I'll have these terrifying urges, like wanting to jump from the balcony of a high floor or just dart into traffic. It’s been really hard to function at work, or anywhere for that matter."
D008-D001_h024.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D008-D001_h024.answer: B & A. Bipolar I Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D008-D001_h025.question:
Lately, things have been a real rollercoaster. For about two months, I was on top of the world, sketching new designs at lightning speed, but then I'd just snap at my wife over the smallest thing. I felt this intense, restless urge, like I just couldn’t sit still, constantly needing to be *doing* something. During that time, I also made some questionable choices, things I normally wouldn't even consider, which really strained my marriage.

Then, for the past three months, it’s like I’ve hit a wall. All that energy just vanished. I’ve been pulling away from everyone, even my closest friends, and just don't have the interest in connecting anymore. Sleep hasn't been helping; I could sleep for hours and still wake up feeling completely drained, like I hadn't rested at all. My mind feels foggy too; I’m constantly misplacing things and forgetting little details, which is frustrating for an architect. Sometimes, out of nowhere, I’ll get this terrifying urge to just step into traffic or jump from a building, even though I don’t actually want to die. It’s all making it incredibly hard to focus on my projects or even get through the day.
D008-D001_h025.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D008-D001_h025.answer: B & A. Bipolar I Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
